text: Whether the formula ∀x(D(x) → M(x)) is *well-formed* is a question of ___, whereas whether it is *true* is a question of ___. Which pair fills the blanks correctly?
explanation: Well-formedness depends only on the shape of the string (syntax); truth requires interpreting D and M in a model (semantics). The chapter stresses that well-formedness and tautology-hood are mechanical/syntactic checks, while truth is semantic. The other options reverse or collapse the syntax/semantics distinction.
